officialTitle: Perioperative Durvalumab for Resectable Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: A total of 802 patients were randomly assigned to receive durvalumab (400 patients) or placebo (402 patients).
design.notes: Stratified by stage and PD-L1 expression; patients with documented EGFR or ALK alterations excluded from the modified ITT efficacy population.

clinicalQuestion: Does perioperative durvalumab with neoadjuvant platinum chemotherapy improve EFS and pCR in resectable stage II–IIIB (N2) NSCLC?

pico.population: Resectable NSCLC stage II to IIIB (N2)
pico.intervention: Neoadjuvant platinum-based chemotherapy plus durvalumab, surgery, then adjuvant durvalumab
pico.comparator: Neoadjuvant platinum-based chemotherapy plus placebo, surgery, then adjuvant placebo

arms.label: Perioperative durvalumab
arms.regimen: Neoadjuvant durvalumab plus platinum-based chemotherapy, surgery, adjuvant durvalumab
arms.dosing: Durvalumab IV every 3 weeks for 4 cycles with platinum chemotherapy before surgery; adjuvant durvalumab IV every 4 weeks for 12 cycles
arms.doseSourceQuote: to receive platinum-based chemotherapy plus durvalumab or placebo administered intravenously every 3 weeks for 4 cycles before surgery, followed by adjuvant durvalumab or placebo intravenously every 4 weeks for 12 cycles

arms.label: Placebo
arms.regimen: Neoadjuvant placebo plus platinum-based chemotherapy, surgery, adjuvant placebo

publications.title: Perioperative Durvalumab for Resectable Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer.
publications.label: First interim EFS analysis / final pCR analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: the stratified hazard ratio for disease progression, recurrence, or death was 0.68 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.53 to 0.88; P = 0.004) at the first interim analysis. At the 12-month landmark analysis, event-free survival was observed in 73.4% of the patients who received durvalumab (95% CI, 67.9 to 78.1), as compared with 64.5% of the patients who received placebo (95% CI, 58.8 to 69.6).

The incidence of pathological complete response was significantly greater with durvalumab than with placebo (17.2% vs. 4.3% at the final analysis; difference, 13.0 percentage points; 95% CI, 8.7 to 17.6; P<0.001 at interim analysis of data from 402 patients).

safety.description: Adverse events of maximum grade 3 or 4
safety.sourceQuote: Adverse events of maximum grade 3 or 4 occurred in 42.4% of patients with durvalumab and in 43.2% with placebo.

strengths: Benefit observed regardless of stage and PD-L1 expression
EGFR/ALK-altered patients excluded from efficacy analysis
limitations: Design cannot isolate the adjuvant-phase contribution
Patients with documented EGFR/ALK alterations were randomised but excluded from the modified ITT efficacy analysis

clinicalImplications.text: Supports perioperative durvalumab with neoadjuvant platinum chemotherapy as an option for resectable stage II–IIIB (N2) NSCLC without EGFR/ALK alterations; driver testing before neoadjuvant therapy is required.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Get EGFR and ALK results before starting neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy — AEGEAN excluded driver-positive patients from its efficacy population.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 37870974. Gene symbols stripped in PubMed abstract text ('documentedoralterations'); interpreted as EGFR or ALK per trial context and recorded only qualitatively. Later OS publications not ingested.
